utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, I think yesterday I gave some guidance to the annexes up till number 53. I'd like to add a few observations. Again, final decisions well-phrased are not yet there, but first of all, Mr. Re, you provided the Chamber under tab 68 with a document in English and a document in B/C/S. It doesn't seem to be the same document, although the numbers, last four digits, start with 1899, first page. The English translation is taken from U021; whereas, the original as presented in this binder starts with U016 and then 1899.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And they have different dates as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The English has 15th of September and the other one is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, different documents -- different documents often have different dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, the one is approximately twice as thick as the other one. I did your homework, Mr. Re. I checked whether it's all right in e-court. In e-court it's okay. But I couldn't say that I was very amused when I found out this late at night that I have to compare the originals and see whether these are the same documents or not. But therefore in e-court nothing needs to be changed, but in the binders we'd very much like to have the original corresponding with the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now that it's been brought to our attention we, of course, apologise for that oversight. But now that it's been brought for our attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- we will immediately rectify and provide the Judges with a paper copy of what's in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now 72. It was already brought to your attention that the report, the first part is not translated into English. That was brought to your attention in the response by, I think, Mr. Emmerson's response. Have you received meanwhile for 72, the first part, a translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will make an immediate inquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because the response dates already -- since you just said once now brought to our attention. This was brought to your attention in the response by Mr. Emmerson. He says part of the translation is missing and that was last week when he filed that response. Or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was not a response. It was the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again, it's something we just overlooked and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- in the paper here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then in addition to a few -- yesterday I said something about the hesitation of the Chamber. And, again, I apologise for not being in a position to -- to find time to deliberate on all matters, to reach final conclusions with all Judges where reading takes us till rather late at night. Yesterday, especially in relation to 17 -- annex 17, annex 18, and annex 25, I expressed our hesitations to admit that into evidence. One of the important reasons being that major portions of these annexes deal with the acts and the conduct of, in that case, Mr. Brahimaj mainly. Now, I noticed and -- that in annex 61, page 7 and page 8, we find also references, although not being the -- I would say the -- the main portion of the document, but on page 7 it goes to the acts and the conduct of the accused Ramush Haradinaj as a participant in attacks on MUP members at four specified locations; similarly, at the top of page 8, you'll find specific reference to act and conduct of a person by the name Toger. Annex 62 - and perhaps I should have mentioned for 61 the MFI number, which was P993. 62, P994, on page 5 we find at the top of the page specific references to Toger liquidating a Serbian prisoner who was detained in the village of Dujak. So, therefore, rather specific act and conduct of a person by the name of Toger. 63 to some extent repeats what we find in 61. If I would take you to page 3, there we find again Ramush participated in attacks on MUP members and the same locations and Toger throwing bodies into the Radonjic Canal we find further down. So these are very specific reference to acts and conduct of the accused. So at least for those portions, you could not be surprised if we would not admit that as evidence through this witness, through these documents. This may serve as guidance for you for the remainder of the testimony of this witness. And then I take it that we'll receive the 68, the right original, and that we receive the translation of - what was it - the first part of 72. Then finally, one observation: For -- for the next witness, I think there was an application, Mr. Re, for adding documents to the exhibit list. I think two documents. Mr. Guy-Smith has drawn the attention of the Chamber to the fact that most of these annexes were not on the exhibit list. And I wonder what explains the different approach in a specific application for two documents to be added to the exhibit list for the next witness; whereas, I think almost all of the annexes here not appear on the witness list and no specific application to add them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The difference is that the witness here, Mr. Stijovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- is well-placed to explain the source and the origin of all the documents which he has personally selected from going through the Operation Krug documents provided by Serbian State Security. He went through the whole lot, read them in Serbian in his office, and pulled out relevant ones to his testimony. The next one is a lay witness and the two particular statements are not the witness's but MUP documents and we considered it to be within a different class and in light with the Trial Chamber's earlier ruling as to classes of documents. It's just a judgement made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's the introduction of a new criteria, I'm afraid, that if the witness selects himself the exhibits that there's no need to apply for adding them to the witness -- to the exhibit list then. But let's -- I didn't hear clearly, Mr. Guy-Smith, that for those reasons you wanted to exclude these documents from evidence. But at least it's a procedural issue which seems to bother you considerably.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, in fact it is, and something that I -- that I raised early on because of the concern that we had with regard not only to the issue of -- of notice but the issue to adequately prepare for the case and the cross-examination of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That come -- that come to the Chamber. As a matter of fact, I would seek to exclude any documents that are not a part of a 65 ter application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you seeking or you would seek?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let's -- I am seeking, to make life easy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber will see what to do with this briefly introduced request. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I mention briefly that in respect of the documents that the Prosecution proposes to adduce through the next witness and that is the subject of the application that Your Honour has just referred to, the Defence will be opposing the admission of those documents through that witness and indeed objecting to certain portions of the witness's 92 ter statement. We have a written objection which is to be filed within the next hour. It won't be filed in the form of a formal motion because of the scope of it, being relatively narrow and a matter that could be dealt with in the form of an out-of-court meeting if Your Honour thought that appropriate, but it should be available to the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution within the next hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that is -- that is a matter that is joined by certainly the Balaj team. It's a matter we're trying to expedite in a fashion to have -- it's simply come to you by -- from one party, as opposed to three parties, but we join in the specific concerns that have been raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: As do we, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Well, at this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not insist on the formal motion on these matters and chooses a -- or at least accepts that the Defence chooses a very practical way of dealing with the matter as long as it is transparent in the transcript what has happened. Now, I have one final observation to make. I'm just trying to find the relevant document. Yes. Mr. Re, if you'd look at 54. 54 says that it is an unofficial translation. I think the attention has been drawn to that as well by the Defence. I wondered, the person who made that unofficial translation, do we have meanwhile a -- an official one or -- because the -- the use of the language is rather surprising. It's sometimes almost phonetic in -- for example, if you look at the third line under the statement, it says: "Regarding this matter" which ... "We are not aloud" in the fourth line from the bottom of the first large paragraph, "aloud," a-l-o-u-d, rather than a-l-l-o-w-e-d. It's a very special way of treating the English language. And I wondered -- it's full of that kind of, well, funny spelling, if I could say so. And -- and, of course, that raises some questions as to the quality of the translation as such. I don't know who made the translation, but I've serious concerns about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I, of course, hear what you say. But I've -- I have to make inquiries. I don't know whether it's been officially translated. I would guess not. It's a resources issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We had to get these ones translated internally within the Office of the Prosecutor because of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. I do understand. But when I read it, I see that apart from that it's announced as an unofficial translation, that it is a translation which immediately shows major flaws in the use of the English language and then perhaps some proactive approach might have been appropriate. I've drawn your attention to it. The translation needs -- "O.V.", I do not know what "O.V." means. "Unofficial translation by O.V." at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not sure I'm looking at the same document. What's the -- you said 54.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 54, yes, report. Annex 54, which it is statement given by Izet Zenuni taken on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P985, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, we'll request an official translation. It's not a -- it's not a difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then are you ready to continue your examination-in-chief of Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Stijovic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While the witness is coming, annex 71, which is MFI P1003, inquiries have revealed that there is no translation of the report. The translation was requested only of the statement. But we will request -- request a translation of the report as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or do not tender the report. That's another solution to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will make that decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- a little bit later, if Your Honour doesn't mind. But, Your Honour, can I just note that the time is slipping by. It's almost 9.25 -- 9.24, in terms of my being able to get the -- elicit the information I need to finish the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do understand. But at the same time, Mr. Re, some of these issues should not have taken time in court, as a matter of fact, but should have been resolved out of court even without intervention of the Chamber. But I'm aware of it, that you lost 25 minutes, partly due to the Prosecution itself and partly due not to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My concern is, of course, getting to the stage where there is information I need to get from the witness and I just can't get it out because of the time. That's my concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. My concern is precision by the parties in what they present to the Chamber at this moment, and, of course, also your concern. That goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, good morning. I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Re will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to turn to paragraph 37 of your -- of your statement which you have with you. It refers to the ambush of a police patrol on the 28th of February, 1998 in Likoshan in Drenica. It was one of those matters which the Trial Chamber requested you to give some evidence about. And for the Trial Chamber's benefit, I refer you to -- refer the Chamber to Jakup Krasniqi's statement and annex 8, which relates to communique number 43 in Mr. Krasniqi's statement and his testimony. Now, my question to you, Mr. Stijovic, is: What was your source of information -- tell the Trial Chamber about your information about your information about the ambush on the police patrol in Likoshan in Drenica on the 28th of February in 1998.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first piece of information I received about this event was through a pager. At that point in time, I was in Decani and on a pager I received information that a terrorist attack was launched in Likoshan and that I had to return to Pristina as a matter of urgency. As I returned to my workplace, the first reports from the police had already arrived about the event, the incident that took place in the area. I mentioned this incident yesterday. This was an ambush set for a police patrol. In essence, this was merely a decoy -- or rather, a point of attracting more groups of police force and four police officers were killed on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your information about who carried out the attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information we received from one policeman who was wounded and another who survived the attack, and from those who came to assist them, was that they were ambushed. They had been driving a Lada Niva vehicle at a bend, at an intersection, they came across an ambush and gunfire was opened on them. In the exchange of fire, they realised that they were up against a large group of armed men with masked faces. That was the first information we received. Fresh police forces were deployed to that area and they conducted searches there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you receive any information about who these -- who the large group of armed men with masked faces were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite precise, I have to explain this in a couple of sentences, if you'll allow me. From mid-1997, we organised covert TV recording of the facility of Jashari compound. From the police station that was immediately above the Jashari compound, we had placed a TV camera there for surveillance, and it was from our premises in Srbica that we were able to follow what was going on there. Immediately before this incident and after the activities resulting from there, we registered a large group of men, including Jashari, leaving the Jashari compound. We recognised on this video recording his brother. There was Sami Lushtaku [phoen] there too, as well as two men from the Kodra [phoen] family. Several hours after this attack was launched, the same group of men returned to the Jashari family house, where they fired shots in the air to express their general celebratory atmosphere. By tying up the information we had -- and I apologise once again for both yesterday and today, but I tend to speed up when I'm deep in thought. This secret TV surveillance was the means of providing us with the most evidence as to who and how organised these actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Page 11, Line 21, the witness explains, I think, that following the exchange of fire fresh police forces were deployed to that area and conducted searches there. I wonder if -- if the witness might explain where he means the searches were conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It will certainly assist in a better understanding. At the same time, I urge the parties not to intervene in the cross-examination -- in the examination of the other party to the extent possible. You've heard that Mr. Emmerson would very much like to know who conducted -- who conducted searches where exactly. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can this be displayed in Sanction while that's coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The police sent additional forces there to assist the police forces that were ambushed. Upon the arrival of the police force on -- in an APC, as is customary, the police engaged in searches in -- of the general area. These are the -- the surrounding villages around Likoshan and they went also in search of the perpetrators. These were the villages around Likoshan and Likoshan itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the people observed coming and going from the Jashari compound and then firing shots -- firing shots in the air expressing general celebratory atmosphere, were they KLA people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Adem Jashari was a prominent member of the KLA, and the group around him had a decisive impact in the growth and thriving of the KLA in that general area at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next sentence, you said -- you referred to several more attacks in Srbica municipality and elsewhere took place thereafter, resulting in the deaths of several policemen and destruction of property. Now, if you're referring to the KLA being the perpetrator, please tell the Trial Chamber what you know about those attacks.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the searches conducted by the police, after the perpetrators -- systematic attacks were organised against the police stations and the police forces in the general area where the ambush in Likoshan was organised. The -- with the primary purpose of spreading out the forces of the police, attacks were launched in the area of Klina, Djakovica, and Decani too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you give the Trial Chamber some facts, what you know about these attacks and examples of these particular attacks you referred to in your statement.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a specific example now, but it's absolutely sure that in the attacks that were launched on the 2nd of March, 1998 that the police courts in Celopek, Klincina, and Rznic were under constant fire. By looking at the time line of these events, one can clearly arrive at this conclusion. Automatic weapon fire, sniper fire on the police forces in the area, this is the information I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask what you mean by "constant fire"? How constant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we had information that from the 1st of January through to the 30th of November, 1998, 1.486 attacks were launched and organised, then we can safely conclude that there were around two to three attacks daily in the area of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the figure could have been 486. The interpreter isn't sure. The witness said: "However, as time went by, the attacks grew in intensity."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: When -- I know it's statistics, please, but you were referring to the 2nd of March.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I spoke of the 2nd of March, Your Honour, and said that the attacks were carried out in the area of Glina, Djakovica, and Decani. These were the attacks where police squads were targets, as well as the family homes of the Serbs living in the area. The objective of these attacks was, as far as we were able to conclude and as far as I, as the chief of analysis, was able to conclude and was able to report to the competent bodies, was to spread out the police force, to divert their focus onto other areas rather than to the areas where the -- the attack was to be launched in effect at Likoshan. This was all -- these -- there were families living in the area. There were the police station at Klincina, at Celopek. I can guarantee that some of the police stations, such as in -- the ones in Celopek, Klincina, Rznic, that they were under constant attack. When I say that, I mean that we had reports of gunfire and attacks on the police force almost on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Re, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please turn to annex 35 in your bundle there, which is Exhibit MFI P96 -- sorry -- I'm sorry, 34 is what I wanted to look at. 966. It's a KLA communique, number 42. And you reference -- reference that in paragraph 35 of your statement. There's just one -- one portion I wish to take you to. It's a KLA communique published in Zeri i Kosoves on the 5th of March, 1998. The date of the communique is the 27th of February, 1998. In the English, it says: "On the 13th of February, 1990 -- I should say 1998. The original says "1998". Mustafe Kurti, a collaborator with the occupier was liquidated." For the Trial Chamber's benefit, that's also referenced in Mr. Krasniqi's statement, at P328, annex 7, the same document published in Pristina Vojka [phoen] on the 25th of February, 1998, at annex 7 of his statement. Can you tell the Trial Chamber anything about the liquidation of the collaborator, Mustafe Kurti?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything more specific about this person. I can tell you about the murder of Desimir Lasic, though. I can tell you about the report on his murder. This person was killed. Now, why, I really can't remember now or explain. I can see in this report the name of Desimir Lasic. I can tell you who this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The communique describes him as "criminal Desimir Lasic, a close collaborator of Arkan, and it says: "On the 23rd of January, 1998, our units carried out an attack on him." What can you tell the Trial Chamber about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely untrue that he was a close collaborator of Arkan's. He was a functionary in the local authorities. He was a member of the executive board of the Assembly of Srbica. He was a prominent public figure, and I believe that he was killed in Josanica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's other microphone be switched on, the interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After this -- this was a village near Klina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I believe that he was killed in Josanica. After that - and this has to do with the latter part of my yesterday's evidence - the police erected a check-point in the village of Josanica. This village lies along the Klina-Srbica road. It's absolutely untrue that this is a criminal or a close collaborator. He was a serious man of education, even an assemblyman of Srbica. He was described in this way only because he was a Serb -- or rather, he was killed only because he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you go to the next annex, please, which is 36 -- I'm sorry, 35. The wrong one. It's MFI P967. It's a State Security report of the 3rd of March, 1998, described as an official note. It relates to the Krug operative action. I just want to take you to one part of that, and that's referring to an attack on the 1st of March, 1998 at around 1600 hours. It's page 2 in the English: "Siptar terrorists opened fire from automatic weapons on the vehicle of Lada type and killed Slobodan Prascevic from Jakovica who had only recently a retiree of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia." What do you know about the attack on the Slobodan Prascevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I ask the Trial Chamber to move into closed session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session. That means that the audience will not hear your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please move to paragraph 41. It's another statement the Trial Chamber -- sorry, another paragraph the Trial Chamber requires more information from you about. And this is referring to the attack on the Haradinaj compound on the 24th of March, 1998. Please be aware the Trial Chamber has heard a fair amount of evidence about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have heard a lot of evidence. Mr. Re, you say the Chamber would like to hear more. I think that the Chamber expressed that on the basis of the evidence already heard, one could wonder whether it assists the Chamber to hear secondhand hearsay on the matter in addition to what is already known.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please turn to paragraph 42 of your statement. And I want to take you to annex 44, which is Exhibit MFI P976, which is an official note of the Prizren State Security Department sent on the 30th of March, 1998. I want to take you to the first paragraph, in which you say: "The Djakovica" -- which it says, sorry, "The Djakovica SUP public security department sent us operative piece of information stating that about 200 militarily trained well-equipped members of a terrorist organisation are in the area of the Jablanica village. The organisation consists of individuals from the village of Jablanica and neighbouring villages, as well as some persons from -- who found a refuge there after the MUP action in Drenica. At the helm of this organisation is a terrorist staff situated in the village mosque in the centre of the village with a fixed radio station." I just want to ask you about the source of the information which has gone into that official note, and in particular about the estimate of 200 militarily trained and well-equipped members of a terrorist organisation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official note is an authentic document of the State Security Service, compiled on the basis of the daily report of the Djakovica SUP. This is information that the public security service collected through fieldwork on the activities and actions of the KLA in the area of Jablanica. In essence, the information contained therein was not fully consistent with the information that the State Security Service had, but it was nothing new to us. As concerns the -- the estimate of 200 militarily trained and well-equipped members, at that point in time we contemplated the figure of 50 to 150. Let me tell you this about the figure: It's a very relative matter in this case, because the KLA already at that point in time developed its organisation at two levels. It developed operative corps containing the small number of extremists who were together every day and did not disperse, and broader territorial grassroots organisation made up of their supporters in the various villages where the groups were active. The figure provided by the Djakovica SUP, in my opinion, is relatively higher than the number that the State Security Service considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the difference in the sources the State Security was relying upon vis-a-vis those relied upon by the Djakovica SUP and why do you assess the State Security sources to be more accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the substance of work of the State Security Service and public security service, it is clear that the State Security Service had much more detailed knowledge about Albanian terrorism. The sources of the State Security Service were solely the sources that were involved in the KLA activities or the persons who in some way were close to the KLA establishment and were able to get direct information from the spot. As for the sources used by public security service, they gathered information about activities on the ground through their own sources, which mostly focused on dealing with crime, which is the main focus of public security service. So it means that their sources were the people who, due to their criminal activities, to their criminal misconduct, had contact with police. As for the State Security Service, we recruited people specifically in order to infiltrate them into the terrorist establishment. As for the regular police, the public security service, they had different sources and the sources were from that area. Another thing that we need to point out is that the information was verified by State Security Service on a much more detailed level as compared to the verification of information by public security service. And you can see that through many of the documents. You can see that public security service forwarded its information to the State Security Service to be further verified and analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the issue of assessment of the strength of the KLA, can I take you to annex 51, which is MFI P982. And that's a State Security Department official note regarding a preliminary interview dated the 15th of June, 1998. And in that document - that's at page 4 of the English, which I think is at page 3 of the Serbian - it says: "The source states that there are around 600 armed members of DTG in the villages of Babaloc, Gramocelj, and Glodjane. During a recent attack on the police members, they were joined by 1400 terrorists from the neighbouring villages." I want you to comment on the accuracy of that particular figure based upon the information available to you at the time and the sources available to you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation and this document, they were made in June of 1998 and they deal with the events which took place in March of that year. So from March to June, as I have said yesterday, as time went by, as the spring arrived, there was an increase in the delivery of terrorist equipment and arrival of terrorists from Albania to Kosovo. Their numbers kept increasing. So from March onwards in Jablanica the number that we had at the State Security Service was between 50 and 150. As time went by, the number increased, because Jablanica, together with Glodjane, became logistics centre to which KLA members from abroad and from other areas of Kosovo and Metohija came and from there they moved to Albania. So the number of over 1.000 terrorists, that figure in my mind is accurate, if we are referring to June.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please move to paragraph 48 and annex 55 of your statement, which is a statement of a person whose name I won't use publicly dated -- taken on the 12th of August, 1998, an official -- and an official record of the interview dated the 18th of August, 1998. The particular part I want to take you to, I think is at page 7 of the Serbian but is at page 9 of the English, and it refers to, at the top of page 9, the first paragraph, some names and a faction -- this faction of the KLA has its -- has its supporters in the municipality of Decani with chief holds in the villages of Istinic, Gornji Strellc, Donji Strellc, Belle [phoen], Papracane, Dubovik. In order to recruit as many KLA supporters as possible, the so-called government of the Republic of Kosovo established barracks in the village of Papracane, the commanders in the barracks at Rrustem Tetaj and Tahir Zemaj, former JNA officers." Is that particular passage referring to what's known as the FARK?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just underneath that, there's another passage which says: "Since two months ago, training for special units, Black Eagles at Crni Orlovi, has been provided on this training ground. There are about 50 or 60 members of this unit there. Ibrahim Ukadaj [phoen] from Crnobreg municipality of Deqan is the head trainer. He's aided by five or six former JNA officers." And he's talking about a staff and a military training ground in the village of Papaz about 15 kilometres away from the headquarters in the mountains. Is that the same Black Eagles as the one headed by Idriz Balaj, or Toger, or a different one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, apart from the fact that the question is leading and -- and there's at this point no particular evidence with regard to the statement just made, but the damage has been done. He could ask an entirely different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This man was the chief analyst of the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It doesn't matter whether he was or not. The question is -- the question as asked is improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re -- Mr. Re, a leading question is a question which includes a matter not yet established. And from what I understand, the implicit factual statement that there was an organisation, Black Eagles, headed by a specific person has not yet been established through this witness. And to that extent, it's leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's in his statement at paragraph 50, and it's also in Mr. Balaj's pre-trial brief at paragraph 14 where it's on the record in his own pleading that Mr. Balaj was the leader of the Black Eagles. It's in the witness's own statement. I'm merely asking the witness if it's the same organisation he's referring to that's being referred to in that document. That can't be leading. It's already on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In paragraph 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It says, paragraph 50: "Our intelligence indicated that Balaj, aka Toger, commanded a KLA rapid-reaction unit called the Black Eagles." I'm merely asking if it's the same one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I missed that. I missed that. That is part of the 92 ter statement. So under those circumstances, you could ask the witness whether when he referred to the organisation he learned about through his intelligence is the same one as he just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You heard the question, Mr. Stijovic. Please answer it for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the same organisation. If you need additional explanation, I can provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there two Black Eagles? Is that what you're going to tell us? No, that is leading. I'll accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please explain, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within the armed formations organised by Albanian separatists, there were two groups. And there existed great rivalry between them, which exists to this day and has repercussions in Kosovo and Metohija even nowadays. NPK supported the KLA and TSK supported the FARK, which was the government of Bukoshi. The popularity that KLA had in that area at the time and their strengthening position was such that it bothered the Democratic League of Kosovo and their leader, Bukoshi. In that sense, those forces, together with the assistance and encouragement from the government of Albania, tried by means of FARK to limit the power of KLA or rather, to put the KLA under their control. And that was the essential rivalry that existed between these two organisations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I feel there may have been a cross-wire in the question and answer, because the witness is being asked about two organisations, that is, subgroups of units by the names of the Black Eagles, and he's answered questions about the KLA and FARK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The one does not necessarily exclude the other, but it needs, certainly, clarification. Let's -- perhaps, Mr. Re, you seek this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there more than one group called the Black Eagles?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those groups in Kosovo and Metohija, it was quite customary to use such names, so there were many groups with similar identical names in the area of Drenica and Podujevo. In this specific case that you asked me about, this group, the Black Eagles, was in Rznic within the KLA under the command of Balaj and then there was another group called the Black Eagles in Albania in the village of Bataj and that group belonged to FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is that -- the second one, is that the one referred to in that official note I just referred you to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, moving to paragraph 50 of your statement, which you provide some information about Toger, your intelligence that he commanded a KLA rapid reaction unit, and you described the uniforms, their insignia, their arming. The Trial Chamber requires some information about one sentence there in relation to your intelligence, where you've said that he was widely regarded - that's Idriz Balaj - as being under the direct command of Ramush Haradinaj. The Trial Chamber wants to know how you can say that, what's the source of your information, the quality of your information, and the reliability of it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hundreds of documents passed through my hands, documents obtained through live sources in which there is very accurate and detailed information about the Black Eagles and the relationship between Balaj and Ramush Haradinaj. Idriz Balaj during that period of time was basically a bodyguard of Ramush Haradinaj. He and his group were constantly by the side of Ramush Haradinaj. Idriz Balaj in that period of time, in late March, April, and early May, when the local staffs of the KLA were established in villages, would always accompany Ramush Haradinaj, and his presence and the number of his forces were such that they represented a sort of a threat to Albanian population in those villages. The presence of Idriz Balaj and armed people around him enabled Ramush Haradinaj to take part in establishment of terrorist groups in the villages around Glodjane and to directly affect the selection of leaders and staffs of the KLA in those villages. Hundreds of documents passed through my hands detailing this and the role of Balaj. He was a bodyguard of sorts, the right-hand man.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Chamber needs to know the sort of information you were receiving and how you were able to assess its quality and reliability to make the statement that Balaj was basically the bodyguard of Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will paraphrase some dozens of documents that I had in my hands. Ramush Haradinaj would come to a certain village with a group -- with a large group of people accompanying him. Alongside, right next to him, was always Ramush Haradinaj or his brother -- rather, alongside was Idriz Balaj or Daut Haradinaj. In that village, they would call a meeting of prominent residents where they would discuss the establishment of the KLA's staff. In that context, the leading role in appointing and selecting the staff members belonged to them, and the information that we received indicated that such an activity over a period of time changed its nature in a way. In those meetings, Ramush Haradinaj would typically ask the villagers to arm themselves and to collect money, to raise money for weapons. Whoever was able to provide money and also willy-nilly people gave money. There were some people who were poor, who had to sell their livestock in order to raise funds to buy weapons, because if they refused to take part in that process of arming, they would have been ostracised in the village. It is also important to stress that the weapons were bought in Albania through some persons who basically turned this into a criminal activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, now you -- you're explaining not only the quality and the reliability of your sources but you continue to explain what your sources told you. Now, for example, selling your livestock. How many instances were reported to you of selling livestock in order to be able to contribute financially to the KLA? So I'm not seeking whether it was cows or goats but how many instances? Was it reported --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that any police leaders in that area can give you exact numbers as to the information you're seeking. The information that we had indicated that there were poor people in basically every village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But my question was: The frequency of such reports, people selling livestock in order to contribute financially to the KLA. Was there one such a case reported to you? Were there five? Were there fifteen? Of course, I'm not asking whether it was ten, eleven, or nine, but whether it was an incident or whether it was frequent -- well, let's say, 10 to 20 such cases or were there 100 cases that were reported to you? Could you give us an indication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It certainly wasn't 100. We treated this as a security phenomenon. And "phenomenon" means that we registered between five and ten such cases. A large number of Albanians didn't dare report a situation where they were faced with a threat. We treated this as a registered security phenomenon. That was our term for such instances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, that raises a question. You are saying that a large number of Albanians didn't dare report a situation where they were faced with a threat. There are two possibilities: Either they did not report because there was a threat or they didn't report because it didn't happen. That's not easy to establish, I take it. Would you please comment on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right. If a leading authority -- if a figure of authority says that this is no time for politics but, rather, time for waging a war and if such a figure of authority tells them that Albanians have to enter into a struggle, they have to wage combat in order to gain freedom and liberation, then people can either come up with opposing arguments showing that they disagree with that, in which case that would possibly lead to a blood feud with other Albanians. And people shied away from that. That was the typical course. However, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This, at least in my understanding, does not lead to a conclusion that a larger number of people sold their livestock in order to financially contribute and did not dare to report that. That's -- that's quite a different conclusion. What you're describing, as a matter of fact, is that there existed a situation and people were urged to support war, not anything else. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to look at annexes 61, 62, and 63. Those are Exhibit MFI P992 -- no, not 992. 993, 994, and 995 are the three. And they relate to an interview with a source whose name I won't mention publicly, but I'll just notify the Trial Chamber and the Defence that that particular statement in annex 63, P995, is -- has a different -- a slightly different translation or part of it in P921, which was marked for identification on the 17th of September, 2007 in relation to the -- the death of Rade Popadic and the police report there. What I'm interested in - and the Trial Chamber has some concerns about these three particular documents which are sourced -- referred to in paragraph 50 of your statement - is the assessment of the statement of this person and the reliability and the accuracy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber said, as a matter of fact - let me just check - whether -- and I refer to specific paragraphs -- whether this is a suitable way of introducing this evidence in relation to those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, I appreciate that, but I wish to ask the witness about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- the reliability of the particular component of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not the concern of the Chamber. But nevertheless, if you'd like to further inquire into any facts in relation to the reliability of this, you are entitled to do so. Please proceed. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply wanted to make the observation in respect of these -- these particular annexes that they do concern and include matters relating to both conduct alleged against the accused and charges on the indictment. And may I therefore urge Mr. Re to confine his questions to matters of fact rather than in the form in which the question was just asked, a general appreciation of reliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, for other portions of the documents it could be important for us to know or to get further information about the reliability, which is a separate issue from whether specific acts of the accused could be proven by this kind of documents. These are two different matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- my fault. I didn't make my position clear. It -- it's a question of establishing material information, rather than assessments of a witness as to his reliability of a source as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did the DB assess the reliability of the -- of the information provided by this source? And by that I mean how reliable was this person? What sort of contacts did the DB or State -- or the MUP have with him, had he provided information in the past, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the first page, under the entry "Information about the source," you can see at the bottom that it says: "Source unreliable. Information verified -- or confirmed." So the assessment of the State Security person -- of this person as a source was that this source was unreliable. This qualification of "unreliable" meant that sometimes this person provided accurate information and sometimes inaccurate. In this particular case, the information was confirmed through other sources of the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let me just -- we are looking at this moment at 61, if I'm right? Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just go back. You said a moment ago that it said information -- "source unreliable. Information verified or confirmed." Can you please look at the Serbian. The English translation says: "Source unreliable- information unchecked." Can you just read the Serbian words, just read the Serbian and they'll be translated.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Source unreliable - information confirmed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, there seems to be then an -- either a translation error. Could we have P993, the B/C/S version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can that please not be displayed publicly as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then not publicly but -- and could someone see -- I take it that from a distance no one could read the -- what is on the screen of the witness. At least, I couldn't read that from 4, 5, or 6 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I could -- we could show it to the interpreters in the booth, if it assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's on the screen already. Could we zoom in the right, a little bit further down. Yes. Are the interpreters -- can they see the line just read by the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Source unreliable - information confirmed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we need a better translation for the first page of this document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that -- excuse me -- in this particular case, the information was confirmed through other sources of the service. I want you to elaborate on that and tell the Trial Chamber about the elaboration by other sources in the service and how that enabled you to make your assessment that this particular information there was reliable.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A source is the person -- in this particular case, the source was actively -- directly involved in the KLA activities and a lot of the information provided by him was already known to us. It had to do with the KLA activities in the territory of Albania and also the support that it received from other structures. That was already familiar to us. We also knew about the activities of the KLA in Krusevac village, Glodjane, and in other parts, as referred to by this source. We also had information that in June, in mid-June of 1998 two persons were abducted, Vucic Vukovic and Novica Vujisic. They were abducted near Zlopek, that's a village, and a Muslim, Izet Gutic was abducted with them. We had this information from before. These people are listed as missing. Vujisic and Vukovic were relatives and Vukovic's property was stolen. I'm now speaking based on my recollections. So this statement provided by him was consistent with information we had already had. This person was sued or put on trial. A statement was provided by him pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure, Article 151/2, and proceedings against him were instituted. An indictment was issued, and so on. I didn't really follow what happened to him afterwards in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a particular passage in the witness's statement I want to take you to, and that's at page 3 of the English in Exhibit MFI P993, and that's the reference to the -- it says: "I also know about a month ago -- a month and a half ago Nasim Haradinaj and his group amongst whom there was a certain Velium [phoen] from Rastavica captured two policemen in Rastavica who were bringing food to Junik. The captured policemen were taken to the staff in Glodjane and following their questioning they were executed by a terrorist with the nickname Toger. Toger threw their bodies into the Radonjic Canal." "Toger's real identity is known only by Ramush Haradinaj and he continuously keeps company with him. Toger trains the special police unit in Glodjane which has 20 members. Listening to him speak, his accent leads me to believe he's from the area of Drenica." Now, what -- you said a moment ago that other sources had confirmed the information in the statement was reliable. What were the sources -- did the other sources confirm that particular piece of information was reliable? And if so, what were those -- what were those sources? What did they tell you? And how did you know it was reliable?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the abduction of the police officers from Sabac SUP is concerned, Popovic and Jovanovic - I believe his first name is Nikola - I believe that they were abducted on the 24th of May on their road to Junik. They were carrying food supplies. They were part of the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Chamber has heard evidence about that, the abduction. What I'm interested in is the information about Toger's involvement in it after the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before -- before we do that, Mr. Re, one of your previous questions included whether this source had been given information before. That was part of your question as an element of reliability. Could you tell us whether this source, was this the first time this source gave information or did he give information at any prior occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this was the first time. This person was arrested by the police, and through the investigation the information was reached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the statement was given when he was still under arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you -- did you speak to this person yourself, the person who was arrested and gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know those who did take the statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there are signatures in the document, I can try to identify them. Evidently, since this is the location, we can see it here, I suppose it was the operatives of the Pec DB who talked to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The signature's on the last page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that that's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last -- could you guide me to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the Serbian, it's on page 3 of MFI P995. In the English, on page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It very much looks as if that's the signature of the person who gave the statement, rather than the person who took the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There are three signatures there. One says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where? Let me just -- we are still on 61?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, we're on 63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I apologise. Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just look at the last page of annex 63, which is MFI P995. There are three signatures there. Do you know the -- the two people who signed underneath the deponent of the statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell exactly who the operatives were, although this first signature -- we had an operative working in Pec whose first and last name started with M.C. Those were his initials. We can see that the signature is quite short and it is possible that this is the operative I'm talking about. I can't identify the second signature, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did -- you said you have his initials. Do you know his name? Are you able to tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. It's not a problem at all. But I can't claim that he was the person who signed the document, but he was the only one who had these initials, M.C. Milo Calic. He was the State Security operative in Pec. "M," for Milo; "C," for Calic. We can see that the last name is quite short and this led me to believe that this was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, just going back to my earlier question. I'm interested in the accuracy or the reliability of the statement there about the involvement of Toger in disposing of bodies in the canal. Did you have any information to confirm or to verify or to corroborate the information in that witness's statement? And if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, the State Security Service had great difficulties in identifying Toger, because in the KLA staff in Glodjane and in Ramush Haradinaj's presence there were two persons who used the nicknames of Tigar and Toger. These names were oftentimes mixed up in the reports that we received. After a while, we concluded that under the pseudonym Tigar there was a person with the last name of Nimani. I believe that he was the commander of the military police within the staff of the KLA led by Ramush Haradinaj. We concluded that Toger was a person exclusively connected with special operations. This was the person who had taken part in war activities in the former Yugoslavia. His accent indicated that he was not from Metohija but from the area of Drenica, and after a while -- .

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The bodies in the canal. That's what I'm asking you about. Did you have any verifying information? If so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read a report or a statement. I can't really pinpoint what it was. I know that this report clearly indicated that Toger personally killed the Vujosevic sisters in late June. These were two elderly sisters. And that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I'm interposing an objection at this point because of the vague nature of the information that's being given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, having read a report, I don't know what it is any more, is not a very solid basis for ... I'm looking at the clock. Mr. Re, you said you lost 25 minutes. We are already ten minutes past 10.30, which is the usual time in which we have a break. So therefore, to wrap up, that would be 15 more minutes and then you would have been compensated for all of the 25 minutes. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour's calculations are spot on, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that you have another 15 minutes after the break. We'll have a break until five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, we have limited time, so please keep your answers nice and short. Before the break, I was asking you about additional information or verifying information connecting Toger - that's Idriz Balaj - with bodies in the canal. Now, can you just please move to paragraph 57 of your statement in which you refer to the DB having information about the killings and the kidnappings of civilians and their disposal in Lake Radonjic canal before the Serb forces retook the area by force. Then you say: "For example, DB Pec report dated 26th of June, 1998." Now, we've just referred to that one, the interview with a suspect, and that was in Exhibit P933 -- sorry, 993, 994, and 995. My question is: Is the information in paragraph 57, is that the additional verifying information you are referring to or is there other information which isn't in your statement which connects Toger with bodies in the canal?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, are you just referring to the first sentences of -- of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, the entire paragraph, everything that's in the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question is whether there's anything additional to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, the question as phrased is somewhat misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I would hate to mislead the witness. If it's unclear, perhaps Mr. Stijovic could tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first important pieces of information about these events started arriving in early June. As of June, we had a constant inflow of information, including the one that persons were killed and thrown, dumped into the Lake Radonjic and the canal next to the lake. We had information from family members - I believe it was the Vlahovic family - to the effect that their parents were still alive a month, a month and a half after their abduction. This was confirmed to them by their friends, Albanians. We checked up on the information and confirmed that it was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was anything additional in relation to -- connecting Idriz Balaj, or Toger, with bodies in the canal, apart from that which you've put in paragraph 57 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a significant number of documents identifying Idriz Balaj as the most responsible person for the attacks, murders, and other events -- incidents happening in the area. All the most serious criminal activities were carried by Idriz Balaj and his closest associates. The very name of Idriz Balaj instilled fear and was perceived as a threat among the population. I mean the Albanians, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Move to paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether he came across any of these documents. Because we've seen a lot of reports and statements, et cetera, in which I did not find until, I think, the 1st of September any reference to -- or perhaps I may be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I saw a great many documents. And I have to use the opportunity to say that I'm sorry that the documents are not here. When I was invited for the first time in the month of July to appear in The Hague, I found it surprising and even horrifying that the documents relating to Krug were not in the possession of the OTP. I know of many other such documents and pieces of evidence about the activities in that period of time. Since I was immediately involved in the organisation and directing of the collection of evidence of the crimes committed in Kosovo, both against Albanians and Serbs, I was the one in charge of that operation for the entire area of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the -- the witness, when he answered your question, referred to the Vlahovic issue, statements that they were still alive. Now, I remember that I came across the Vlahovic issue, I think, once when going through the documents, but unfortunately my memory leaves me there, and I would like to verify what is the date of the document in which the possible -- possibility that the Vlahovics are still alive exactly is, so that I can better understand. If anyone could help me. I know that I came across it. But I haven't learned all the documents by heart yet. No one? Then I'll try to find it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We'll check into that and get back to you. Can I just -- in relation to what Mr. Stijovic just said, alert the Trial Chamber to the fact that the Operation Krug documents which we requested, we have disclosed the entirety of those which we received from the Republic of Serbia. I think it was in July/August, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Moving to paragraph 58, Mr. Stijovic, and that's where you say: "The DB had a source present during a meeting in Papracane during which Rok Berisha stated that: "The fish in the Radonjic lake are feeding on human flesh." He also said that: "Lake Radonjic would never be a proof of Albanian masculinity but a disgrace for the Albanians." This is one of the portions of your statement the Trial Chamber requires further information about, and in particular where you say you had a source. Now, can you name the source in open session or can you tell us the nature of the source in open session? If necessary, we'll move into private session if you can tell us who the source was.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a live source, a person who took part in the large meeting held in Papracane in the second half of August. The service used this person as an associate. That's why I wouldn't be able to give you his full name. I don't even recall his pseudonym at this time. I do, however, remember this formulation because it's quite characteristic -- or rather, the name of the person uttering these words at the meeting is quite characteristic. I can explain the circumstances in which the meeting was held and what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're more interested in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re -- yes, one of the -- one of the risks here is that the same information from the same source comes through various channels but finally is only one source, and that's, of course -- that would be of some concern to the Chamber. If you would be in a position to seek further clarification on whether that risk exists, yes or no, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you only have one source present at the meeting who provided the DB with this information about the fish in Lake Radonjic feeding on human flesh?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This formulation was uttered by that one person. We had several persons present at that meeting on the basis of which we came by the full information on why the meeting was held in the first place and what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you a moment ago whether -- I think you said you can't remember the name of the person, that -- that particular associate. Can you -- can you remember how many people the -- were at that meeting had provided information to the DB?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three to four sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they KLA members?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that these persons were supporters of the KLA. One or two of the sources were members of the FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did the information each of them was giving compare? Was it inconsistent or consistent or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information was consistent save for the part where Rok Berisha was mentioned, this formulation. Now, as for the contents of the meeting itself, the information was almost identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could move to paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is there any way seeking confirmation of whether Witness 17 was among the sources? That should be done in -- in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In -- the Trial Chamber has also raised some concerns about paragraph 54. Can you just please read that to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can that please be displayed in Sanction. And it starts off by saying: "During that time, in June and July 1998, Ramush Haradinaj, as KLA commander in the named zone, sent through orders -- written orders to a large number of KLA members in the village of Lodja to pursue further terrorist activities." I just want to point you to several exhibits on the exhibit list. Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 593. I'm just simply to ask -- asking you to identify whether these are the KLA orders you're referring to which you refer to in that statement.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this isn't that order. This is a list of persons. The image I have in front of me on the screen, a list of 21 persons who received weapons. This was signed by Ramush Haradinaj. And at the end of the list, it says: "Sent to the files, the archives, and the staff in Lodja." So this isn't an order. In the upper right-hand corner, it says that it was sent to the staff in Lodja. But it's not an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, it seems I'm -- I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From now, five minutes, and then it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one I'll show you is P -- 65 ter 583, the 7th of July, 1998. Is that one of the orders you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I please get a number just -- just MFI is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as P1011.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is MFI -- sorry, P -- 65 ter 589.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Same question: Is that one of the orders you refer to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. May that also receive a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as P1012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown also MFI -- sorry, 65 ter 2078 and 2079 but not displayed publicly. These are witness statements and subject of the amended -- the application in respect of the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: These two documents are expressed to be statements of two particular people. I just want you to look at those two documents and tell me if they are statements given to the MUP. And if so, I can get them marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is coming now. Likewise, is that second document also a statement given to the MUP, 29th of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May those two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says "SUP." I do not mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: SUP is the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: SUP is the MUP. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's one part of the MUP. It's the public sector for security. May those two please be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: With consecutive numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 02078 will be marked for identification as P1013 and 65 ter number 02079 will be marked for identification as P1014.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The decision on whether they can be added to the exhibit list is still pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The final question I want to ask you is in relation to your statement about the Serbian people who -- at paragraph 59, where you said: "By May 1998 no Serbs or Montenegrins remains in Dasinovac, Ratis, Ljumbarda, Papracane," et cetera, et cetera. Can 59 please be displayed in Sanction. And yesterday you said there were 800 families -- Serbs living in the area before 1998. What was the source of your information about the number of Serbs living there before and the number of Serbs living there by May 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source of our information was the statistics kept for each municipality. And these were not 800 families but 800 persons, including elderly and children. These were persons living in the centre of Decani and in the surrounding villages. By the month of May, all the rural parts inhabited by Serbs and Montenegrins were left without any Serbs or Montenegrins. The people were either driven away, abducted, or in any way compelled to leave the area. There was no room for them there simply because they were Serbs or Montenegrins. Later on, as the KLA grew stronger, the same fate befell the villages around Klina. In the month of June, the same happened to the villages gravitating towards the municipality of Pec. They were also free of any Serbs, Montenegrins who were driven away, forced away. And wherever there was the presence of the KLA, there were no Serbs or Montenegrins. This was true not only for the area under the control of Ramush Haradinaj but this was true of all the area -- areas under the control of the Liberation Army of Kosovo at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Before I invite Mr. Emmerson to start cross-examination, Mr. Re, we earlier this morning had a brief exchange of views on amendment of the exhibit list. May I bring to your attention the decision the Chamber issued on the 25th of May of this year. It was a decision on amending the 65 ter exhibit list. And specifically, paragraph 6, which reads as follows: "In relation to the documents concerned by the motion, such as pseudonym sheets or maps, the Chamber agrees that the flexible approach to introduce such documents described by the Prosecution is suited to trials of this kind and does not compromise the rights of the accused. However, as conceded by the Prosecution response, paragraph 6, if any new documents are of substance nature, a formal motion for amendment of the Rule 65 ter exhibit list will be in order. The Chamber will then decide whether any such document could be presented and tendered before it on the basis of the parties' submissions and the law." That means that the criterium is not who selected the documents but whether documents of a substantive nature could be added to the list. This is just to remind you. Mr. Emmerson, may I invite you to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Stijovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, I want to start, if I may, by asking you some general questions about the organisational structures of the RDB and of which the RDB was a part. Now, I've understood your -- your position correctly, I think, that you remained in Kosovo until the 12th of June, 1999. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1999. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you are in a position to help us with these questions about institutional relationships throughout 1998 and 1999, I take it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a member of the State Security Service, and you're asking me about matters for politicians, and I'm not sure that I'll be able to give you clear and precise answers to that. I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's see how we get on. The overall head of the RDB, the State Security Service, from 1991 until October 1998 was Jovinka [phoen] Stanisic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from October of 1998, was that post then taken over by Radomir Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
