utterances.text: Mr. Markovic had been a senior official within the RDB for a number of years before he took that post as head of the RDB, had he not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you -- can you help us, please, as to what his post was during the period that we've been discussing up to October 1998.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the public security sector, and I believe that he was the assistant minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia. He had never worked in the State Security Service before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic was for a period of time in prison in Serbia after the conflict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Radomir Markovic is still in prison in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just tell us, please, why he's in prison in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of criminal proceedings are pending against him for abuse of official authorities and other law-sanctioned activities. I can't really specify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come back to that, if we may. Now, you told us in your testimony last week that all information within the RDB in Kosovo flowed through the analytical department and therefore across your desk at one time or another. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the way the flow of information went, then this should be true. I believe that all information reached me, which does not rule out the possibility that there was a parallel illegitimate channel of information. Therefore almost all the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that there was a parallel illegitimate structure for the supplying of information within the RDB?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the RDB -- I don't think so. When I said "a channel," I primarily meant that a telephone line may be used. That's to say, senior officials of the RDB may cross the security line and pass some information over by phone whilst there's a piece of paper that goes up the hierarchy structure in the organisation. That's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's what you meant when you referred to a -- the possibility of a parallel illegitimate channel, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you about a man called Goran Petrovic. What post did he have within the RDB and when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2001 in the month of January, Goran Petrovic was appointed chief of the State Security sector of the Republic of Serbia; that's to say, of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, after Radomir Markovic was removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, prior to his appointment, had he been within the RDB or in some other part of the apparatus?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of 2000, he was thrown out of the State Security Service. This was either in 1999 or 2000. Therefore, he hadn't been part of the State Security Service for one or two years. And earlier on, in 1998 and in early 1999, he was a member of the State Security Service at the post of the head of an operative group in the department of the State Security Centre in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In a sentence, if you will, please, do you know why he was thrown out?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, he was accused of misconduct at work and revealing official secrets. Apparently, there was an intercepted phone call that he sent to the media. I don't know if that was the actual reason, though.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the other microphone for the witness please be switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we then just understand the institutional relationships very briefly. The RDB was a part of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, or MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And during 1998 and 1999, the Minister for Internal Affairs in overall charge of the MUP was Vlajko Stojiljkovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, help me if I understand this correctly. The ministry consisted or two divisions: The public security division, or the RJB, and the state security division, or the RDB; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the public security division during the period we're concerned with was headed by General Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've already told us that Mr. Jovinka Stanisic and then Mr. Radomir Markovic headed the State Security division. And very broadly speaking, the RDB's responsibility was counterintelligence and counter-subversion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you again, please, in one sentence summarise what the overall responsibility of the RDB was.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RDB was in charge of counterintelligence affairs, intelligence affairs, and internal security, the three spheres of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, again, some questions for asked earlier on about SUPs and MUPs. Can we just clarify that briefly. In Kosovo - and I'm focusing now on Kosovo, rather than Serbia - in Kosovo, individual police stations were referred to as "OUPs"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Kosovo and Metohija are part of Serbia and part of the single system of the Ministry of the Interior, both when it comes to public security and state security services during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I be clear. Individual police stations would be organised around regional centres known as SUPs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And SUPs were responsible for coordinating all ministry activity, that is, MUP activity, within their area of responsibility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you wish me to explain, I can explain, but the answer is "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Can I ask you a specific question first: Were the SUPs responsible for liaison and support for units of the RDB within their area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And hence, for example, we see at Djakova police station RDB officials working side by side on the same investigation, sometimes interviewing the same suspects as their colleagues from the public security division; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the SUPs until June of 1998 reported to a body known as the MUP Staff for Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that's correct, but you're speaking of the public security service; thus, I'm hesitant. I think it's correct. There was a staff in Pristina headed, I think, by General Lukic, to which secretariats of the interior were subordinated, but I'm not fully certain that that's how it was in the formal legal sense, that that's how it was organised within the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did the RDB have an involvement in that structure?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did the RDB come to have an involvement in that structure later in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify that question. What do you mean "involvement"?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, were there RDB officials within a joint structure for the MUP Staff in Kosovo under the command of Sreten Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you just help us, please. I'd like you to be handed a -- a black file of documents which I'm going to use with you in cross-examination. And can I indicate that for the time being, Mr. Stijovic, you can put the black file you've been using to one side. We'll come back to some of the documents in that a little later on. But for the time being, I'm going to ask you some questions about documents in the file that's about to be handed to you. Could you turn in that black file, please, to tab 19, which is Defence document identification 1D620139 and is not yet marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this is a document dated the 16th of June signed by the minister, Mr. Stojiljkovic, establishing a ministerial staff for the suppression of terrorism in the area of Kosovo and Metohija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just look down the list of staff, it is headed by Major General Sreten Lukic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, 16th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did I say 1999? I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you did --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, 1998. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the immediate deputy on this joint body to Mr. Lukic is David Gajic, somebody you told us was your superior and the chief of the RDB in Kosovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A few moments ago I asked you whether the RDB came to have involvement in the joint structure under the MUP, and you told us that they did not. Can you just help us. Did you not know about the existence of this organisation or -- or -- or what was the basis for the answer you gave us on page 59 between lines 12 and line 20?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me -- I agree. Perhaps I didn't pay attention fully to your question. In June, a staff was established for suppression of terrorist activities in the area of Kosovo and Metohija. This is the first time that I see this decision on establishing this staff. This is the first time I see this document. And it was then that a joint operation started to suppress terrorism in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. If we keep looking -- if we continue analysing this decision, you can see that after David Gajic the people listed on this page and on the other page are all from public security, except for Milorad Lukovic, who was assistant chief of staff for special operations. And in the last sentence of paragraph 1, on the following page it says that in the -- "The expanded staff shall also exclude [as interpreted] chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs, centres and branches of the RDB." And this pertained to the period of time from June to end of August. This is the first time I see this document; however, I agree with what is stated here, especially in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just help me. At page 59, at line 11 and following I asked you whether there was RDB involvement subordinate to General Lukic in the joint structure, and you said no. And then I said: "Did the RDB come to have an involvement in that structure later in 1998?" And you asked me for clarification. And I said: "Were there RDB officials within a joint structure for the MUP staff in Kosovo under the command of Sreten Lukic?" And you said no. Now, just -- just so that we understand the position, when you gave that answer, did you in fact know that there was such a joint staff or -- or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was a staff, but I, as chief of analysis department, wasn't interested in that staff and its composition. My duty was to gather information from the field and to inform David Gajic about that. That's why I told you that this is the first time I see this document. I know for a fact that from late June until late August there was a staff for suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija, because there is an official report submitted by that staff about its activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned Milorad Lukovic as being the Assistant Chief of Staff for special operations. Milorad Lukovic is also, I think, known by the name of Milorad Ulemek and by the nickname of Legija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By your leave, however, Your Honours. May I? I didn't know that he was assistant head of staff for special operations. He worked for the public security service, and this is the first time that I see that he also had this title within this staff, that he was assistant head for special operations within that staff. When I mentioned the names, I mentioned David Gajic as head of the service, and I said Milorad Lukovic. All other people belonged to the public security. He at that time was commander of the unit for special operations, and he was a State Security member, and I knew him as such. This is the first time I hear that he was assistant head for special operations in that staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you -- you mention him as a commander of a unit for special operations as part of the public security division. I just want to be clear. If we can --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Sorry. Then I've misunderstood you. Was he within the State Security sector, the RDB, or within the public security sector, the RJB?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: JSR, units for special operations existed within the State Security, the RDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I wanted to clarify. We'll come back to that in a moment or two. Let's just get the picture absolutely clear. The public security division, that is, the RJB, had two special units officially, known as the SAJ and the PJP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you -- could you please explain to us, first of all, whether the SAJ and -- and the PJP respectively belonged to the public security division or to the State Security division.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SAJ and PJP belonged to the public security service, the RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly the question I asked you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think we've got the answer clear now. The JSO belonged to the RDB, your sector, did they not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they're sometimes referred to at the time as the Red Berets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the public, yes, that's how they were known, under that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, we've heard evidence that by April of 1998 they had a base near Deqani monastery 2 kilometres east of Istok, can you confirm that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain that it was by April. I think that it was until October. After the Holbrooke-Milosevic agreement was signed, the unit was pulled out of that area and it was located in a facility or in several facilities across from the Deqani monastery, some 2 kilometres from Deqani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And that organisation was under the overall command of a man called Frenki Simatovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, when the witness says he doesn't know whether it was by April --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could you please further explore whether it could have been earlier or later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm going to do that in just a moment, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you look behind tab 2 in the black file, where you will find a combat report signed by Colonel Dragan Zivanovic as chief of staff of the VJ 125th command in Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, already in evidence or needs a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is not yet, I think, in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number 1931.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just look, please, at item number 5 in that report. Colonel Zivanovic records - and this is 27th of April, to remind you - "During the day, a sabotage and terrorist detachment of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, including all their equipment and two MI-24 helicopters, the so-called Frenkijevci arrived to the area of Deqani and Istok. We have personally got in touch with Simatovic, Frenki. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That word "Frenkijevci" or Frenki -- I don't know whether I'm pronouncing it correctly. Frenkijevci, does that mean "Frenki's Boys"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that's what it means, but this term was used in this report, and, yes, in -- publicly that's the term that was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, by your leave, may I address you? I don't want anyone to misunderstand me. The gentleman asked me whether they were there until April of 1998. At least, that's what I heard, whether the unit was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, then there must be a translation error or some other kind of misunderstanding. What Mr. -- Mr. Emmerson asked you is whether they were there by April. Then I now better understand your answer, that you said they were there until October. You may have misunderstood the question or it may be misinterpreted. Could you tell us on from when. Was it from April or any earlier or any later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came to the Deqani area in April of 1998 and they withdrew in October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I told you where they were located, headquartered.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Brazil Group of the JSO, can you help us please -- you won't find it in the document at the moment, not in that document, but have you heard of the Brazil Group of the JSO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally for the moment on -- on this topic, Milorad Lukovic, what was his command position in relation to the JSO in Deqani?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Lukovic was superior to a part of the unit located in Deqani. And that part of the unit was headed by Colonel Radojica Bozovic, a member of the JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, so that we're clear about this, you, no doubt, are aware that the overall commander of the JSO, Frenki Simatovic, and the overall commander of your organisation, the RDB, in 1998 are jointly indicted by this Tribunal for war crimes committed in Croatia and Bosnia. That's something presumably you are aware of.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there is a proceeding before this Tribunal in which Frenki Simatovic is mentioned. You can correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask you what you knew about the details of what the allegations involve in just a moment, in terms of the structure of your organisation, but the indictment is IT-03-69, and the joint accused are Jovinka Stanisic, the head of your organisation at the time we are concerned with, and Franko Simatovic, the head of the special forces of your organisation at the time we are concerned with. And I'm just going to read to you a very short extract and ask you what you know about this aspect of your organisation's functioning, if anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this. The -- the indictment against Mr. Simatovic and Stanisic is, from memory, from the end of 1991 until the middle of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: They're not indicted for anything that happened in Kosovo from 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I fail to see the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll explain the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They're indicted for establishing a series of irregular paramilitary groupings which were brought within the overall control of the RDB and committed unregulated crimes on the ground, some of which subsequently, we submit, and we'll show, found their way into Kosovo. And what I'm asking about is the integrity of the RDB's organisation and those who were at the head of it in using criminal paramilitaries as operatives on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The relevant passage in the indictment, Mr. Stijovic, reads as follows: "From no later than May 1991, secret units which were not legally authorised were established by or with the assistance of the Serbian DB for the purpose of undertaking special military actions in the Republic of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you're quoting from what?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 3 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Leaving out parentheses.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "These units included but were not limited to groups known by the following names: Red Berets, Skorpions, Arkan's Tigers, also known as Arkan's Men or Arkanovci, Martic's Police, the Militia of the so-called Serbian Autonomous District of Srpska -- Baranja -- I'm sorry, of Slavonija, Baranja, and Western Sujen [phoen]. The JSO, the Jedinica Specijalne Operacija, and the JATD." Paragraph 5 alleges that Mr. Simatovic had responsibility for these special units of the RDB and directed their involvement in operations in Croatia and Bosnia. And my question for you, Mr. Stijovic, is: What do you know about with your own service establishing illegal paramilitary formations under the authority of the head of the service and Mr. Simatovic prior to 1998, first of all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I know that the JSO was within the RDB starting from 1997 or 1998. Formally legally speaking, the JSO has been part of the state security from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would 1996 in fact be the correct date, Mr. Stijovic? For the creation of the JSO as part of the RDB?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's difficult to verify that in the archives of the RDB within the MUP. I don't know the exact date. But if you say that it was in 1996, I can accept that. You probably have documents confirming that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you knew nothing, despite the seniority of your role and your security clearance that you gave evidence about, you knew nothing about the creation of the JSO out of paramilitary groups that had been operating in Croatia and Bosnia? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no paramilitary groups active in Kosovo and Metohija, and I was so busy with the activities of Albanian extremists and terrorists in Kosovo and Metohija that I had absolutely no time to look into the events in the former Republics of the SFRY. That was not within my scope of work, nor was it within the scope of work of the part of the RDB to which I belonged.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. But you were in a very senior position within this organisation, you tell us, Mr. Stijovic. What I'm asking you is: Is it really the position that you knew nothing about the relationship between your own organisation and the paramilitary formations that had operated in those two republics?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for attributing such importance to my position, but I think I'm in a better position to judge my own importance. I was head of analysis department in Kosovo-Metohija and I was dealing with that. As to the events in 1991 through 1995 I was an operative. And then from 1996, I became head of the analysis department. And then I dealt with the events in Kosovo and Metohija from 1996 through 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, if Mr. Emmerson asks you whether you knew something or not, just tell him whether you knew or not. You don't have to explain why you knew or why you didn't know unless Mr. Emmerson has a specific interest, and then he'll ask further questions on the matter. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, at page 70, line 7 your answer is recorded as follows: "There were no paramilitary groups active in Kosovo and Metohija." Now, do I understand your evidence to be this, that during 1988 -- I'm sorry, during 1998 and 1999 there were no Serbian paramilitary groups, that is, irregular illegal paramilitary groups operating on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how you can understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll turn to that in a moment or two, please. Could you look, please, behind tab 4 in this bundle. I want to ask you to comment on certain aspects of a report that concerns the disbanding of the JSO. Milorad Lukovic, also known as Milorad Ulemek, also known as Legija, was arrested in Serbia in 2003 for the murder of Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And having been convicted of the murder of a number of members of the Serbian Renewal Movement, he's currently serving a 40-year prison sentence in Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation wasn't good. Can you please repeat the question or your comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it correct that he is currently serving a 40-year prison sentence for the murder of politicians in the Serbian Renewal Movement or officials from the Serbian Renewal Movement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A sentence was -- or a judgement was rendered in that particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And immediately after he was arrested, is it right that the JSO was disbanded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to just do a fact check with you, please, on some of the material in the report that you find behind tab 4. And I'll just read short passages to you and ask you to help us with your knowledge, either to confirm or contradict what is there recorded. First of all, "the Serbian government has announced that it is disbanding the elite police force, the special operations unit JSO with immediate effect. The decision followed the arrest on Monday of an assistant commander on the unit -- of the unit on suspicion of having taken part in the assassination of Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic two weeks ago." This report, as you see, is dated 26th of March, 2003. Does that refresh your memory as to whether the JSO were disbanded following the arrest of Mr. Lukovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps the term itself was something I found controversial. The government of Serbia did pass down a decision to disband the JSO; however, after detailed vetting, a good many members of the JSO became part of the gendarmerie of the MUP of Serbia. Therefore, all those who had not been involved in criminal activities did not take part in all of that that was of interest to a court of law became members of the gendarmerie, because among them there were many honourable persons, honourable fighters. When you said "disbanded," I understood that to mean fully disbanded, where people were sent home. Just to make myself quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your organisation's existence was terminated and some of its personnel transferred to other posts. That's the position, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You said among them, there were honourable people, as distinct from those involved in criminal activities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were honourable and honest people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you then to just help us with the next section in this report. And for the -- for the record, this is Defence document 1D62-0006. And may that be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that, will be marked for identification as D169.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The JSO -- I'm quoting to you the passage now: "The JSO was formed in 1996 out of a group known as the Red Berets which was set up by Serbia's security service in 1991, shortly before Croatia's declaration of independence. The purpose of the Red Berets was to fight alongside, as well as to arm, train, and coordinate the activities of various Serbian paramilitary formations in Croatia and later in Bosnia-Herzegovina." Pausing there. Were you aware when the JSO was set up that it had been effectively formed from the organisation which was previously known as the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not my part of the job, the personnel structure within the RDB. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about your job, Mr. Stijovic, specifically or your area of responsibility. I'm simply asking you whether as an official -- and it was Mr. Re's examination of you which established your importance in the hierarchy -- whether an official at level 3 or 4 or 5, as you told us, in the RDB, whether you really were in ignorance of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was the hierarchy in Kosovo, not the hierarchy in Belgrade. That should be made quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- yes. I think there could hardly be any confusion. Did you know? Did you not know? Mr. Stijovic, that's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And continuing: "Many of these paramilitaries were run by gangland bosses. The best known among them, the late Zeljko Raznjatovic, or Arkan. In the process of establishing and maintaining the Red Berets, the long-serving head of the State Security Service during the Milosevic era, Jovica Stanisic, managed to establish a degree of control over Serbia's expanding criminal underworld. But with the Red Berets recruiting many hardened criminals, the symbiotic relationship between Serbia's secret police and Mafia bosses increasingly turned into an uncontrollable and unreliable force." Now, again, can I ask you, please: When these men under the heading or title of the JSO and the command of Mr. Simatovic and Mr. Lukovic were deployed in April 1998 in Kosovo, were you aware that they had connections to criminal gangs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, by your leave, I don't know what the gentleman is quoting, where he's quoting this text from, the text which suggests what their actions were. And then the questioner follows: Did you know about this? As if what the gentleman quoted was indeed the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, first of all, I'll -- what Mr. Emmerson is doing is he's quoting from a report which appears under the heading "BBC News," that's so that -- what was published at the time. I agree with you, Mr. Stijovic, that Mr. Emmerson, asking about awareness of a certain fact, better could ask you whether you heard or learned about such things, which leaves open whether this reflects reality, yes or no. If he would like to know whether you know anything about whether these things really happened, then I think Mr. Emmerson will specify that question and then will also thoroughly explore your source's knowledge, because that was an issue in your testimony on from the beginning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I accept the correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, were you aware in 1998 of allegations that the special forces of your own organisation were peopled by criminal elements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's something that had never been brought to your attention at the time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to tell me specifically what you're referring to. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you, please: Do you know what the expression "deep wedging and burning" means?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have to -- Mr. Stijovic, now your answer is: "You have to tell me specifically what you're referring to. I didn't know." Now, knowing something has different levels. Mr. Emmerson asked you whether allegations ever came to you. So that is to say, whether anyone ever said it's a bunch of criminals or whether anyone ever said it's just Arkan's men or ... Mr. Emmerson is now asking not about knowledge of the reality but, first of all, he asks you whether it was ever brought to your attention that such allegations - whether true or not - were there. And by answering saying "I do not know," the answer should be: I never heard about it or I never learned anything about it or, of course, that you did hear or did learn about it. Let's try to keep matters entirely clear in this respect. Did you ever hear about such allegations? First, in general terms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When did you hear about them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you'll allow me, Your Honours. There is quite a difference between the questions put by the gentleman and the question put by you, because he is making a connection between the burning and torching and my organisation. You asked me whether I had heard of criminal activities, such as torching, in general and that's why I answered "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the last question, Mr. Stijovic, could not raise any such confusion because the only thing Mr. Emmerson now asked is: When did you hear about them? Could you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Albanian mass media portrayed all the activities conducted by the police as terror and excessive use of force. In this regard, the Albanian mass media reported in detail on all -- on the police activities. They referred to them as "criminal police activities," which involved torching, murder, plunder, and such-like activities. There were such incidents -- incidences, and we received reports of individual isolated incidents of the sort on the ground, such as theft, stealing money from civilians, but these cases were processed through a justice administration. Cases were instigated for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Could we just look behind tab 5 for a moment, please. And this is D165. This is a report again by Colonel Zivanovic of a series of operations up to the 8th of August, 1998. If you look at the very last paragraph in the report, on the second page, he refers to some of the units involved and he refers to the JSO and a unit of the JSO known as the Brazil Group. I'll read the words specifically: "JSO, particularly the Brazil Group, are very well trained." If you could just now, please, turn to the first page of the document. And in the Serbian, it is about six lines up from the bottom. It is the last bullet point under paragraph 1.2. The report records that: "The Brazil group carrying out deep wedging and burning operations." And I wondered if you could help us as to what in RDB terminology would be referred to as a burning operation on the part of the JSO.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As much as I should like to help you, I can't. First of all, this is the first time I see this report. This is a report from the army. As for Brazil title, I don't know whether it existed. I don't know what the structure of the JSO was and how these teams were -- were organised. Now, as for these words, well, it always depends on the person using these words. These are the ones you should discuss these matters with. Now, as for the terms "deep wedging," "burning" one's way through, I see that as going deep into a certain area, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm -- I want to return, if I may, to an answer you gave a little while ago in answer to questions from me where you said that there were no Serbian paramilitary groups active on the territory -- territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Let me lay the foundation for the next series of questions with you, first of all. I want to ask you about a man called Major General formerly Colonel Branko Gajic, who was assistant chief of the security administration for the VJ. Can I ask you: Did you know of Colonel Gajic, Colonel Branko Gajic, or did you know him whilst you were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him, but I know that he was a very skilful operative of the military security service, highly positioned at the time. I believe that he's retired now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And was your organisation exchanging information with his?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organisation at his level exchanged information in the context of Radomir Markovic. He -- because Gajic was chief -- was deputy chief of military security service, so he was at the level of the deputy chief of State Security Service. Compared to them, I am at an inferior level in terms of the exchange of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the answer is, yes, there were exchanges of information but they were at the level between Mr. Markovic and Colonel Gajic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is customary for intelligence and security information to be exchanged, and I do believe that's correct, what you're saying is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you some questions now about some testimony that Colonel Gajic gave in the Milutinovic trial which is taking place in this building and to see whether you can help us about this, because the information that he gives concerns information supplied by your service. Colonel Gajic testified that he was tasked on behalf of the VJ to investigate the presence of irregular paramilitary groups in Kosovo. Now, he testified that there were such groups, that they were made up of criminals whose aim was violence and looting, and that VJ intelligence discovered a number of paramilitary groups directly linked to the MUP in general, to your service, the RJB, and to the RDB in particular. And he testified that once in Kosovo, these groups would be issued with uniforms of the SAJ so that they were indistinguishable from MUP special forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we have the time frame for the testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- of Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'm going to relate it back to an earlier stage as well. The time frame for the testimony is 1999, but the answers the witness has given cover the entirety of the conflict; that is to say, the answers that this witness has given. The relevant abstract for this first series of questions is behind tab 6, and it's pages 15273 through to 15276 in the Milutinovic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, please, what your service knew about two of these groups in particular. Mr. Gajic testified -- and I'm tab 7 at this point, so pages 15351 onwards. Mr. Gajic testified that he attended a meeting on the 17th of May, 1999 with President Milosevic and with your boss, Radomir Markovic. And he testified that during the meeting Mr. Markovic provided information about a group called the Skorpions, who were under the control of a man called Slobodan Medic, or Boca. He said that this group had been brought into Kosovo by General Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic in March 1999 and that members of the group had committed a massacre at a place called Podujevo on the 31st of March, 1999, in which they killed ten children and two adults. He testified that they had then been removed back to Serbia under an agreement between the VJ and the MUP and that your boss, Mr. Markovic, told the meeting that General Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic then breached the agreement and brought the group back into Kosovo. This is the extracts behind tab 7, pages 15351 to 2. Were you aware of any of this, Mr. Stijovic, going on in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But Mr. Gajic is a serious person, and I do believe this to be true. The investigation I conducted with Radomir Markovic led me to know that this meeting was held with President Milosevic. I don't know the contents of the meeting, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to the investigation you conducted into Mr. Markovic later on in my cross-examination. But so far as the operation of the Skorpions is concerned and the fact that Mr. Djordjevic brought them back to Kosovo after they had -- were known to have committed a crime involving the killing of civilians, that's not something that Mr. Markovic, your boss, obtained from you or that you were aware of.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. You can see that this is at the level of the chief of public security and the Chief of State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask you then about a group that you certainly do know about, because you've told us about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, are we moving to a new group. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We are moving to a new group, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps it's better to have the break now. We'll have the break -- Yes Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one small correction that might be important at a later stage. Page 61, line 19, the testimony as recorded in the text and -- and as I heard it over the English translation - and we're referring here to Exhibit -- or to the tab 19 - the witness read: "The expanded staff shall also exclude chiefs of the secretariat," which didn't seem to make sense. And looking at the original English translation, it says: "The expanded staff shall also include chiefs of the secretariats". As I say, it may become important at a later stage, and I thought we should just clarify that at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember that you read that portion of tab 19? I'll go back with you to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It's on the second page of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- of the Bosnian -- of the Serbian, about halfway down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 61, line 19. Yes, you said the following: "And in the last sentence of paragraph 1 - that was the document you saw for the first time - on the following page, it says that in the -- the expanded staff shall also exclude chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs, centres, and branches." And Mr. Harvey now takes it that you either misspoke or that you misread or that it appears not correctly on the transcript, that you wanted to say and that you were reading that "the expanded staff shall also include." Is that what your recollection is as well from reading at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, yes. It is illogical to say that they would be excluded from the expanded staff. It was either a misinterpretation or some other mistake. Such terminology is used always for expanding something and not saying that something will not be expanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter is then corrected. We'll have a break until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed, but I'd like to inform the parties that there are reasons to try to speed up in such a way that the witness can leave tomorrow after the morning session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when we took more time this morning, not in every respect that added to the evidence given in chief. So therefore the Chamber invites you to try to very much focus and see whether we can finish by tomorrow quarter past -- quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm certainly aiming to -- to maintain that indication from -- from yesterday. I do, though, if I may, wish to pursue one or two questions and one or two topics concerning broader issues than the material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it finally up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, you spoke earlier on in your evidence in chief by reference to Arkan. Presumably Arkan is somebody who you would accept was a criminal element.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Arkan in response to your question, but I don't remember speaking about him on my own, unless you direct me to that part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, if you just could answer the question. The question was whether Arkan is somebody you would accept to be a criminal element.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on his conduct and activities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just look behind tab 8, please, in the bundle. And I'm referring again to the testimony of Colonel Gajic in the Milutinovic case. He is asked at line 11 on page 15379: "The Arkan group, on whose authority did they go to Kosovo? Do you know that?" And he replies: "Yes, the State Security Department. "Who in the State Security Department?" "The department chief. Mr. Rade Markovic, the RDB chief." And then he goes on to explain that they were brought in by Mr. Markovic and sent by the RDB not to the army but ultimately to the SAJ. Were you aware that your boss had brought Arkan's paramilitaries into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you maintain the position that you knew nothing of their presence in Kosovo at any point during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that a group of persons that belong to Arkan's group -- are you referring to Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan? That's his pseudonym. "Arkan" is his pseudonym. There was a group of 200 persons from Western Serbia who were armed and in vehicles, and they attempted to enter the territory of Kosovo near Ribarici, which is near Kosovska Mitrovica. That was in the first half of 1998. They were stopped both by police and the army and banned from entering Kosovo and Metohija as an organised group. They were told that they could not go in in such a manner and if they wanted to come in as volunteers to Kosovo and Metohija, they could apply to reserve forces and enter as such but that they were not allowed to come in as an organised group. That's all I know. And they were sent back. They -- they returned. I know even the name of the person who led them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, this -- this is a reference to a group of Arkan's men being brought into Kosovo by Radomir Markovic, and he explains elsewhere in his testimony that they established a reception centre at Kosovo Polje for these men. Is that something that rings a bell with you at all, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. And had that been a case, I would have definitely known about this, because the State Security Service dealt with organised activities, extremist activities, both of Albanians and Serbs. Such an activity could not go undetected without us knowing about it, especially not in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you said -- "he says elsewhere in his testimony that they established a reception centre at Kosovo Polje."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that here or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In terms of where -- where it's to be found in his testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Your Honour could just give me one moment. I think it's -- I think it's in one of the extracts in the bundle. Yes, it's behind tab 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Page 15274, question from Judge Bonomy: "What did you establish Arkan's Group did in Kosovo?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll find it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when Colonel Gajic testified that it was on the authority of the State Security Department that a contingent of Arkan's men were brought into Kosovo, you say that's not true; is that right? 'Cause you would definitely have known about it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Mr. Gajic is somebody whom I hold in great esteem, but I cannot confirm this piece of information or what he said in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard testimony in this courtroom from Colonel John Crosland, the British military attache to Belgrade, about having seen what he described as "imported thugs" in the area of Deqan during 1998 and having followed them to a base in Montenegro, where they corralled with a very large number of other men in plain clothes. And I'll just take you, if I may, to one passage of his testimony behind tab 9. And I'm referring to the transcript in this case at page 3051 and 3052. He describes having seen these men in plain clothes and in vehicles which looked well-equipped and on occasions with earpiece communications in the area around Deqan and following them, as I say, to Montenegro. And at 3052, line 6 and following he says that his assessment was that elements of the RDB were involved with that grouping. Now, were there plain-clothes paramilitary groups within the RDB operating in the Deqan area in March of 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know who these men may have been that Colonel Crosland observed with earpieces in plain clothes corralling in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I asked you for the source of the establishment of a reception centre --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reason why I asked that is because what I, at that time, saw under tab 8, page 15380, the answer of the witness is: "Our sources registered their presence in the territory of Kosovo Polje. We did not have anything more specific up until the very eve of the meeting held at Milosevic," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, that did not convince me that the testimony said that there was a reception centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you referred me to 6. Now, I find in 6, page 15274.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That you've drawn my attention to, a question by Judge Bonomy saying: "What did you establish Arkan's Group did in Kosovo?" And the witness then answered: "We established that in the centre in Kosovo Polje there was some sort of reception of these volunteers" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Some sort of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and then, however, somewhere else, on page 15275, the witness says: "My answer to this question is that in the case of these three paramilitary formations" -- and I'm just wondering whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they are there -- "they did not go through the procedure according to the orders of the -- concerning the reception, processing, and sending."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a bit unclear to me that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I -- one needs to read the testimony in context. But at paragraph -- in the passage Your Honour has taken -- drawn attention to, 15274, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think there -- I think there was one word which was omitted on the transcript from when Your Honour read from it. "We established that in the centre of Kosovo Polje there was some sort of centre there for the reception of these volunteers. They committed a crime." Now, the volunteers he's then referring to are Arkan's Group. At page 15275 when he talks about "three paramilitary formations," he is referring to Arkan's Group and to two other groups, the Skorpions, which we've touched upon, under the command of Slobodan Medic, and another group, known as the Wolves of Drina. And in respect of all three, the testimony at 15275 is that they were not officially incorporated as they should have been through a proper processing procedure. Now, that's as I understood the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just then check again what you put to the witness here. Yes. Perhaps the "they" in line -- in page 86, line 22 -- "that they established a reception centre at Kosovo Polje for these men" -- yes, whether it was for these men or for volunteers and whether this was specifically for, if I could say so, the criminal volunteers that is not apparent. But, of course, I have to very quickly review the sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I might make more -- I might take more time for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally under this rubric, I want to ask you about a grouping called the Pauk Group or the Spider Group controlled by a man called Jugoslav Petrovic, which is alleged by Colonel Gajic to have infiltrated the 125th Brigade of the VJ, which was then under the command of Colonel Dragan Zivanovic. Are you aware of the existence in Kosovo of a group under the control of Jugoslav Petrovic known as the Pauk Group or the Spider Group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And it doesn't seem logical to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Let me see if I can prompt your recollection at all. This man Petrovic was investigated by your service and reported to be working for the French security services and to have been sent to Kosovo with a mission to deal with the Albanian factor. Does that ring any bells with you, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Jugoslav Petrusic -- it's not Petrovic. It's Petrusic. He's a person who was arrested in Belgrade, not in Kosovo and Metohija. Initially, it was the military intelligence who worked with him. They questioned him about certain events. And later on, the RDB in Belgrade worked with him. Since that was outside of my scope of work, I don't know what transpired with that group and what was their role in the area and whether he was in Kosovo at all and whether he was able to work with the army and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you more generally: Were you aware of complaints or indeed examples in which forces under the ministry, the MUP, were involved in committing grave crimes against the Albanian civilian population and then attempting falsely to implicate the VJ for those crimes in order to cover up their responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of one situation that resembles the one that you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please give us a short summary of what you know in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of Istok municipality -- Istok is a place near Pec. There were some crimes committed against the citizens, against Albanians. There were complaints that there was theft there, robbery, confiscation of money, and then police and the military blamed each other, including local authorities. Following that, a working group was established pursuant to the agreement of everyone involved, comprising RDB, VJ, and RJB, and they were supposed to look into the case and submit a report. That's the only situation that I'm aware of that resembles the one you described.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: These were property crimes, were they? Theft and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's the case. Definitely property crimes. Now, whether there were any other crimes as well, I don't know, but definitely illegal activities and illegal conduct. A report was drawn up about that. And by your leave. It was established that the greatest portion of responsibility for that type of situation and the -- on the ground should be attributed to the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look behind tab 12, please, at a report of Colonel General Pavkovic, the 25th of May, 1999. And in particular, can I direct your attention, first of all, to paragraph 4. "It has been established beyond doubt that we have already -- and we have already reported on it in regular combat and other reports that due to the non-compliance with the re-subordination orders, some MUP members, and to a considerable extent, entire smaller units which operate independently on the ground, are committing serious crimes against the Siptar civilian population in settlements or refugee shelters. Murder, rape, plunder, robbery - aggravated robbery, I think that is - theft, and they then purposefully attribute or plan to attribute those crimes to units and individuals in the VJ." Now, that's obviously a assessment of a -- an ongoing practice which is described as something which has been established beyond doubt and is the subject of regular reports. So my question to you is: The MUP forces involved on the ground in Kosovo, were you aware of this broader allegation that murders and rapes were being committed by those forces and then attempts made to fabricate responsibility, to point the finger at the VJ?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this is the first time I see this document, and I challenge its authenticity. First of all, because it's quite typical to blame somebody else for what happened in Kosovo and Metohija. In this particular case, in May of 1999, Mr. Pavkovic allegedly issues a document in which he explicitly and clearly states that there was such conduct and that it was solely due to the MUP members. He, as commander of the 3rd Army and the army in general, are, according to him, completely innocent of this. There were criminal activities everywhere, both among the Serbs and the Albanians. As for crimes and activities -- crime -- criminal activities by the Albanians, they were committed by the KLA members and FARK members. As for the Serbs, there were members of the MUP, members of the army, and a lot of civilians who were involved in criminal activities. So I doubt and I claim with full responsibility that this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, you said you challenge the authenticity of this document. This is a document produced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, perhaps we'll ask first: Mr. Re, will you join the witness in challenging the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I don't. But perhaps the word "authenticity" could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I think Mr. Emmerson is doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be clear whether the witness is challenging --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the veracity of the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It seems that he's talking about logic rather than --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then, of course, Mr. Re, in the back of your mind, could be that where the witness earlier said that one was blaming the other, that this, of course, was a document that was issued by one of the potential wrongdoers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Stijovic, when you said you challenged the authenticity of this document, are you suggesting that the document is a forgery or are you suggesting that its contents are not true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my position that its content is inaccurate and untrue. I am not able to say anything about the authenticity of the document itself. I'm just referring to the contents, which are not consistent with the situation on the ground, with the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 12, Your Honour, is Defence document 1D62-0135.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It needs a number, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It needs a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D170.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before we depart this document, I want to turn to paragraph 6, please, which reads as follows: "The cooperation between the organs of the State Security Department in Kosovo and Metohija is not good either, as we have not received yet a single piece of information regarding members of the VJ reserve force. The exchanges of operative and other information are few and far between and the information served to us about Siptar terrorist forces is frequently general and inaccurate, leading to the unnecessary exhausting of unit commands and particularly the security agencies engaging in their verification." Can I ask you: Were you aware that VJ military intelligence regarded the information supplied by the RDB as frequently general and inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They expressed doubts, just as we, as RDB, had certain complaints about what they did in relation to infiltration of weapons from Albania into Kosovo and Metohija; that is to say, we had complaints about how well they controlled the border. This document dates from May 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. You -- you have told us that when compiling statistics, that apart from the border incidents which were, I think you said, not properly recorded, you were able to make comparisons between information held by the VJ and information held by your service. I'm just trying to understand how the close degree of correlation you told us about last week fits with the assessment that we see in this report.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't any big differences, especially not as of 1995 onwards, as the intensity of terrorist activity grew.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I want to turn now to ask you some questions about the testimony that you were called to give in the prosecution of Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, earlier you referred to transcripts both of testimony in this case and other cases. May I take it that by reading the relevant portion and pointing at the relevant pages that there's no need further to tender those --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, certainly so far as the testimony in this case is concerned, that is the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to then turn to ask you some questions about the testimony you were called to give in the Milosevic trial. Now, you were called in that case to testify by the Prosecution about an interview you had conducted with your former boss, Radomir Markovic, on the 26th of June, 2001, whilst he was in custody, concerning the finding of a lorry container in the River Danube, which was believed to contain the remains of Kosovo Albanians killed during the conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think, in fact, you interviewed him on a number of occasions between April and July 2001 at the request of senior officials in the RDB. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the task I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you questioned him about wide-ranging issues and allegations of impropriety within the RDB during his period of tenure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So -- so in order to investigate the former head of the RDB's involvement in crime, you -- you, as an RDB official, were assigned that task; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you manage to find out whether he had been involved in crimes orchestrated through the RDB during his period of tenure?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through Radomir Markovic we came to learn a great deal of information about unlawful conduct and activities in the earlier period, whilst he was the chief of State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Unlawful conduct and activities by the State Security Service or by other branches of the Serbian apparatus?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individuals from the State Security Service, individuals from the leadership of public security, Ministry of the Interior, and individuals from political and state leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so far as the officials within the RDB were concerned, were these allegations of involvement in serious crime?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you give us an indication of the sorts of crimes, please, that RDB officials were engaging in, according to your investigation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, I can tell you what types of crime these were, but because of my duty to keep state secrets, I can't tell you details. These are crimes of misconduct, abuse of position, relations with the criminal underworld, corruption, money laundering and such-like.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, essentially, corruption between senior officials in the RDB and the criminal underworld in Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about a huge problem involving the authority in Serbia, the internal corruption within the structures of authority of the Republic of Serbia. This included the police, security officials, statesmen, politicians of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look briefly behind tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is not perfectly clear. Mr. Emmerson, I think you're asking whether this corruption was an interaction between senior officials in the RDB and the criminal underworld in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It included that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the witness said: "We are talking about a huge problem involving the authority in Serbia," which doesn't answer the question. And then he continued: "The internal corruption within the structures of authority of the Republic of Serbia." And he said: "This included the police, security." That still does not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- establish a link between the criminal underworld and the authorities. So therefore, it's not an answer to your question, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I ask you specifically: Did you find evidence of connections between officials within the RDB and criminals in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look, please, behind tab 13, first of all. I'm going to ask you about the interview you conducted with Mr. Markovic in custody on the 26th of June. So not about those wider ranging allegations but about the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not an objection. Can we just move into private session for one moment while Mr. Emmerson is formulating that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before we look at the interview with Mr. Markovic on the 26th of June, behind tab 13 is a document dated the 25th of May which is an MUP summary of an investigation of the refrigerator truck case and describes the background to the recovery of the truck, the circumstances surrounding it being removed, the involvement of General Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic, and the suggestion that bodies were removed from it, and the truck then set on fire and blown up. And if we could just turn, please, in the English to page 3, the pre-penultimate and penultimate paragraphs, and in the Serbian, page 3, the last paragraph over onto page 4, we can see there that a working group had been established to investigate this incident. And the extract reads: "Operative information acquired by the working group indicates that in March 1999, a working meeting was held in the office of Slobodan Milosevic, then-President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The meeting was attended by Vlajko Stojiljkovic, minister of the interior; General Vlastimir Djordjevic, chief of the RJB; General Radomir Markovic, chief of the RDB and others. On that occasion, General Djordjevic raised the issue of clearing up the terrain of Kosovo and Metohija. And in this regard, Slobodan Milosevic ordered Vlajko Stojiljkovic to take measures to remove all traces which could indicate the existence of evidence of the crimes committed." And then it goes on to describe how that was said to have been done, which included: "Clearing up the terrain in Kosovo and Metohija, where there had been combat operations, with the aim of removing civilian victims who could potentially become the subject of investigations by The Hague Tribunal." Now, was it in respect of that part of the investigation that you were then tasked to conduct the interview on the 26th of June with Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know who this brief or information belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is a -- obviously a -- a MUP document, but I'm simply asking you to confirm that that was the purpose of the 26th of June interview with Mr. Markovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that there is a statement I took from Rade Markovic at the time about these activities. But still I don't know whose document this is. It says: "MUP, UKP." But it hasn't been registered under any number. It doesn't bear a stamp. It doesn't say to whom it was sent. I'm looking at the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I have some difficulties in -- as far as the -- your question is concerned. Was your question to ask the witness whether his 26th of June interview served the purpose as set out in this document; that is, that it was -- the interview was held in the context of removing all traces which could indicate the existence of evidence? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Quite specifically the question that I'm seeking confirmation from the witness of is that he was tasked to interview Mr. Markovic about the meeting in March 1999, which is referred to in the pre-penultimate paragraph in the English translation on page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think if I can just pick up -- pick up the witness's last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you turn behind tab 14, the statement that you took is there set out. I'll conclude this topic, if I may, in just a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a quarter to 2.00, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm happy to conclude it at this point and then pursue it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then continue tomorrow because, otherwise, another Trial Chamber will have to wait. Mr. Stijovic, you may have noted when I urged the parties to -- to focus on the most relevant topics that the Chamber is aware of your concerns about leaving. The Chamber will also further inquire into the travel arrangements that have been prepared so to see what is and what would not be a problem as far as your schedule is concerned. I would like to instruct you, as I did before, that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. And we adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 10th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
